result:
Understood. One short step before I write: we haven't touched how it gets built, and that choice shapes the whole document. You've told me what you want, so I'll make the build call. Here are the options I weighed:

**A. Add it to the taproom app you already run (my pick).** It gets new pages and tables in the same Flask app and database on the office Pi. The barcode scanners act like a keyboard, so a scan drops the lot number straight into a form, with no special drivers. The label printer runs from the same Pi. There's one machine, one database and one thing to back up.

**B. A separate batch app on the same Pi.** This keeps brewing apart from taproom tabs. But it means a second program to keep running and a second database to back up, and you get nothing for the extra upkeep.

**C. Off-the-shelf brewery software, or a spreadsheet with a scanner.** This is quicker to start, but the lot numbers end up in someone else's system or a file anyone can overwrite. A bottle-to-sack trace is only as good as the data behind it.

I'm going with **A**. This is big enough to need a proper written design, so I'll save it in the project under `specs/`. The project folder isn't under version control yet, so I'll set that up to keep a record of the design. Before you see the design, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it. If that turns up anything only you can answer, I'll bring it back once, in a single short message.

Unless you'd rather go another way, I'll write it up with A next.
